days.title: Udaipur by arrival — the lake city at palace pace

stops.title: Rajasthani thali near Jagdish Chowk
stops.notes: Dal baati churma, gatte ki sabzi and a rooftop view of the palace wall

stops.title: City Palace and its museum
stops.notes: ₹400 for the palace museum ticket. The Crystal Gallery and the light-and-sound show are separate tickets, sold at the counter

stops.title: Lake Pichola boat to Jagmandir
stops.notes: Day boats run about ₹400; the sunset slot costs more (₹600–800) and sells out first. The boat boards beside the palace

stops.title: Dharohar folk show at Bagore ki Haveli
stops.notes: Puppets, ghoomar and the famous pot-balancing act, in the haveli courtyard every evening. Buy at the gate in the afternoon

stops.title: Night on the lake, Udaipur
stops.notes: Lal Ghat or Hanuman Ghat side — the palace is lit across the water from the roof

days.title: North to Kumbhalgarh — darshan at Nathdwara, then the great wall

stops.title: Shrinathji Temple, Nathdwara
stops.notes: No entry fee. Queues move fastest before 9 AM; phones and cameras stay outside, and the pichwai painting workshops behind the temple are the local craft

stops.title: Lunch in Kumbhalgarh village
stops.notes: Eat before the climb — the only kitchens at the fort are at the gate village

stops.title: Kumbhalgarh Fort
stops.notes: ₹40 for Indian adults at the ASI gate. The wall runs 36 km along the ridge — Badal Mahal at the top is a 20-minute climb, and the last stretch is steep

stops.title: Night below the fort
stops.notes: Resorts here sit in the forest belt around the fort — quiet, and the one place on this trip where you can see stars

days.title: Ranakpur's marble — the deliberately slow day

stops.title: Ranakpur Jain Temple
stops.notes: 1,444 carved marble pillars, no two alike, and no entry fee — a camera or phone charge is collected at the counter. Shoulders and knees covered; no leather inside

stops.title: Lunch at the temple complex
stops.notes: The temple's own dining hall serves a simple vegetarian thali — it is the only reliable kitchen for miles

stops.title: Slow afternoon and night at Ranakpur
stops.notes: This is the trip's rest day on purpose: three fort days behind you, a long drive ahead, and a valley with nothing to tick off

days.title: West to Jodhpur — the long drive, then the stepwell at dusk

stops.title: Arrival lunch at Sardar Market
stops.notes: Makhaniya lassi and mirchi vada at the clock tower end — the market's own food, not the rooftop restaurants

stops.title: Toorji Ka Jhalra stepwell
stops.notes: Free to walk down into — a 1740s royal stepwell that the city cleaned up and handed back. A five-minute walk from the market, so it costs nothing after the drive

stops.title: Night in the blue city
stops.notes: Stay inside the old wall near Nai Sarak — the blue lanes and the stepwell are a walk from the door

days.title: Mehrangarh, the blue lanes and the market before you fly

stops.title: Mehrangarh Fort and museum
stops.notes: ₹200 for a domestic adult — the museum trust's own published rate, and ticket sales close at 17:00. The elevator is ₹50 one way; the ramp up is steep but the courtyards are worth the walk

stops.title: Jaswant Thada cenotaphs
stops.notes: White marble beside the fort road, on the way back down — a small ticket is collected at the gate (see the ticket allowance)

stops.title: Blue-city lanes on foot
stops.notes: The indigo houses cluster below the fort — Navchokiya is the photographers' lane, and locals will point you up the right one

stops.title: Last lunch in the old city
stops.notes: Kachori and mirchi vada on the old-city side of the market — the last proper meal before the airport road

stops.title: Sardar Market and the clock tower
stops.notes: Spices, mojari slippers and bandhani — the last stop before the airport, twenty minutes away

expenses.label: City Palace Crystal Gallery (separate ticket at the counter)
Lake Pichola sunset-boat upgrade (₹600–800 vs the ₹400 day boat)
Small ASI tickets and camera charges not itemised (Jaswant Thada, Ranakpur camera)

publication.title: Mewar Forts & the Blue City — Udaipur to Jodhpur
publication.tagline: Four forts and a marble temple in five days, ending in Jodhpur — one-way, so you never drive the same road twice.
publication.bestSeason: Oct–Mar — cold mornings, clear light and no desert heat. April–June crosses 42°C by noon
travelTips: Fly into Udaipur and out of Jodhpur. Rajasthan circuits are usually sold as returns to the same city, which costs you a wasted day of driving.
The third day is deliberately light. Three fort days in a row is how people ruin Ranakpur by arriving exhausted, and the Jodhpur drive is long enough that the fort deserves its own morning.
Hire the car with a driver for the whole five days; the Kumbhalgarh and Ranakpur roads are hill country, not highway.
Mehrangarh's ticket window closes at 5 PM and the fort needs three hours — start it straight after lunch, not at 4.
Carry cash. Nathdwara, Ranakpur's counter and most Jodhpur market stalls do not take cards.
warningsAndAssumptions: Entry fees checked Sep 2026: Mehrangarh ₹200 domestic adult (museum trust's own published rate), City Palace Udaipur ₹400, Lake Pichola day boat ₹400, Kumbhalgarh ₹40 Indian adult at the ASI gate.
Mehrangarh's elevator (₹50 one way) and audio guide (₹180) are extra and not in the ticket figure. Entry is free for all visitors on Jodhpur Foundation Day (12 May).
Kumbhalgarh's ASI ticket is printed as ₹35 in some listings and ₹40 in others; ₹40 is published here, with the foreign-visitor rate at ₹600.
Ranakpur's temple has no entry fee — a camera/phone charge is collected at the counter, and it is the one stop where leather and uncovered shoulders will turn you away.
Bagore ki Haveli's evening show is priced at ₹130; the ₹60 figure quoted on some sites is the daytime haveli museum ticket, which is a different thing.
Udaipur's Crystal Gallery (₹550) and the Pichola sunset upgrade are listed as optional lines, not baked into the headline budget.
All costs are engine estimates over real coordinates and cited fees, not quotes. Treat ±15% as the honest band.
